newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to start lira ERM talks soon - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy to start lira ERM talks soon - Prodi.

text.p: Talks over bringing the lira back into the European exchange rate mechanism (ERM), will start "as soon as possible", Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said after a meeting with French President Jacques Chirac.

Prodi added that both Italy and France respected each others' recent budgets, which were drawn up in a bid to get their respective economies ready for the planned launch of the single European currency in 1999.
Prodi was furious mid-week after Chirac publicly questioned Italy's fitness to join Europe's new currency from its planned start in January 1999.
Chirac immediately rowed back from his comments and on Friday told reporters there were "no differences" between Italy and France over all the big issues facing the two countries.
He added that the Prodi government was making considerable efforts to clean up Italy's public finances.

The Italian cabinet last week approved a tough financial budget for 1997 which is designed to slash some 62 trillion lire off the projected deficit and meet tough criteria for countries wishing to be in on the start of economic and monetary union. -- Rome newsroom +39 6 6782501
